s: eagerly, readily, with a ready mind
11400.full:
προθύμως
[in LXX: 2Ch.29:34 (יָשָׁר לֵבָב), Tob.7:8, al. ;]
eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: 1Pe.5:2.†
(AS)

11401.full:
ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ
[in Sm.: 4Ki.3:4 * ;]
found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, 1Pe.5:4.†
(AS)

11403.full:
ἐγκομβόομαι, -οῦμαι
(κόμβος, a knot, whence ἐγκόμβωμα, a garment tied on over others, used especially of a frock or apron worn by slaves),
to put on oneself, as a garment, gird on: ἀλλήλοις τ. ταπεινοφροσύνην (as for service, RV, cf. Thayer, see word, but cf. also ICC, in l.), 1Pe.5:5.†
(AS)

11405.full:
ἐπι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
to bear witness to: with accusative and inf., 1Pe.5:12,†
(AS)

11406.full:
συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν
chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1Pe.5:13.†
(AS)

s: equally privileged, held in equal honour
11407.full:
ἰσότιμος, -ον
(ἴσος, τιμή),
equally privileged, held in equal honour: πίστις, 2Pe.1:1 (R, mg., equally precious, but v Field, Notes, 240; Mayor, in l).†
(AS)

s: to bring in or supply besides
11409.full:
παρ-εισ-φέρω
to bring in or supply besides: σπουδὴν π. (late Gk. for cl. σ. ποιεῖσθαι; cf. Deiss., BS, 361), 2Pe.1:5.†
(AS)

11410.full:
μυ-ωπάζω
(μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; μύω, ὤψ)
to be short-sighted: 2Pe.1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; see ICC, in l).†
(AS)

11413.full:
φωσ-φόρος, -ον
(φῶς, φέρω),
light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Isa.14:12, Job.3:9, Psa.110:3): metaphorically, 2Pe.1:19 (see Mayor, in l).†
(AS)

s: to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce
In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly
11416.full:
παρ-εισ-άγω
__1. to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce.
__2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: 2Pe.2:1.†
(AS)

11417.full:
πλαστός, -ή, -όν
(πλάσσω),
__1. formed, moulded (Hes., Plat., al.).
__2. Metaphorical, made up, fabricated, feigned (Hdt., Xen., al.): 2Pe.2:3.†
(AS)

s: for a long time, from of old
11418.full:
ἔκ-παλαι
adv. (of a class of compound adverbs common in late Gk.; see Mayor on 2 Pe, l.with),
for a long time, from of old: 2Pe.2:3 3:5.†
(AS)

11419.full:
ταρταρόω, -ῶ
(Τάρταρος, a Greek name for the underworld, esp. the abode of the damned),
to cast into hell: 2Pe.2:4 (see Mayor, in l).†
(AS)

11421.full:
βλέμμα, -τος, τό
(βλέπω),
a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2Pe.2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)†
(AS)

11422.full:
ἐγκατοικέω, see: ἐνκ-.
ἐν-κατοικέω, -ῶ (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν),
to dwell among: before ἐν, 2Pe.2:8.†
(AS)

s: to fare sumptuously or feast together or with
11424.full:
συν-ευωχέω, -ῶ
to entertain together. Pass., to fare sumptuously or feast together or with: Ju 12; with dative of person(s), 2Pe.2:13 (Arist., Luc., al.).†
(AS)

s: that cannot cease, not to be restrained
11425.full:
ἀκατάπαυστος, -ον
(καταπαύω),
that cannot cease, not to be restrained: with genitive of thing(s), 2Pe.2:14, T, Tr. txt.†
(AS)

11429.full:
κύλισμα, -τος, τό
(κυλίω), [in Sm.: Eze.10:13 * ;]
__1. a roll.
__2. = κυλισμός (which see), a rolling, wallowing (or, as κυλίστρα, Xen., Eq., see 3, a rolling place): 2Pe.2:22 (Rec.).†
(AS)

11431.full:
1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic
2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

11432.full:
ῥοιζηδόν
adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow),
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2Pe.3:10.†
(AS)

11433.full:
καυσόω, -ῶ
(καῦσος, burning heat, fever),
only in pass.,
__1. to burn with fever (Galen., al.).
__2. In NT, to burn with great heat: 2Pe.3:10 3:12 (V. Mayor, in l).†
(AS)

11436.full:
ἀμαθής, -ές
(μανθάνω), [in Sm.: Psa.49:11 * ;]
unlearned, ignorant: 2Pe.3:16 (on the rareness of this word, see MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

11437.full:
στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Isa.3:1 * ;]
__1. a setting firmly, supporting.
__2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2Pe.3:17.†
(AS)

s: Antichrist, "one who assuming the guise of Christ opposes Christ"
11438.full:
άντι-χριατος, -ον, ό
Antichrist, "one who assuming the guise of Christ opposes Christ" (Westc., Epp. Jo., 70): 1Jn.2:18 Jn 2:22 Jn 4:3, 1Jn.1:7 pl. 1Jn.2:18 (cf. ψευδόχριστος, and see MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

11439.full:
κυρία
(Κυρία, T, WH, mg.), -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for גְּבֶרֶת ;]
a lady: 2Jn.1 Jn 5 (on the interpretation, see ICC, 167 ff.).†
(AS)

11440.full:
φιλο-πρωτιύω
(φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.)
to strive to be first: III Jn 9 (eccl.).†
(AS)

11441.full:
Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες
(Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus),
as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jn 9.†
(AS)

11442.full:
φλυαρέω, -ῶ
(φλύαρος),
to talk nonsense: with accusative of person(s), ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jn 10.†
(AS)

11443.full:
ἐπ-αγωνίζομαι depon.;
__1. to contend with (Plut.).
__2. to contend for (C.I., 2335, 19): with dative of thing(s), Ju 3.†
(AS)

s: to slip in secretly, steal in
11444.full:
παρ-εισ-δύω
(also -δύνω),
to slip in secretly, steal in: παρεισεδύησαν (vulgar aor.; pass. for act., El., § 19, 2), Ju 4 (cf. also MM, xix).†
(AS)

11445.full:
δεῖγμα, -τος, τό
(δείκνυμι);
__1. (cl.) a thing shown, a specimen.
__2. = cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, 2Pe.2:6), an example (a warning): Ju 7.†
(AS)

s: a rock or reef over which the sea dashes
11448.full:
σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ
(on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41),
__1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.).
__2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).†
(AS)

11449.full:
φθιν-οπωρινός, -ή, -όν
(φθινόπωρον, late autumn),
autumnal: δένδρα φ., autumn trees (said to be without fruit therefore at a time when fruit might be expected; see Mayor's elaborate note, Ep. Ju., 55-59, and reff. there): Ju 12.†
(AS)

11452.full:
μεμψίμοιρος, -ον
(μέμφομαι, + μοῖρα, fate, lot),
complaining of one's fate, querulous: Ju 16 †
(AS)

11453.full:
ἀπο-δι-ορίζω
(διορίζω, ἅρος, a limit),
to mark off, hence metaphorically to make separations: Ju 19 (Cremer, 806).†
(AS)

11455.full:
Ω, ω, ὦ μέγα (cf. ὂ μικρόν),
omega, ô, the twenty-fourth and last letter. As a numeral, ω᾽ = 800, ω, = 800,000. As a symbol of the last (= τὸ τέλος), τὸ Ὦ (Rec. Ω, L, ὦ, T, ω), the Omega: Rev.1:8 21:6 22:13 (cf. Ἄλφα).†
(AS)

s: Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea
11456.full:
Πάτμος, -ου, ἡ
Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea: Rev.1:9.†
(AS)

s: Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean
11457.full:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ,
Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
(AS)

11458.full:
Πέργαμος, -ου, ἡ
(so Xen., Paus., al., but -ον, τό in Strabo, Polyb., and most writers, also in Inscr.; in NT the termination is uncertain)
Pergamum, a city of Mysia: Rev.1:11 2:12.†
(AS)

s: chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance"
11461.full:
χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό
chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Rev.1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).†
(AS)

11463.full:
Ἀντίπας (T, Ἀντείπας), -α (in some MSS. it appears to be indecl.; but see M, Pro.12:1-28; it is abbrev. from Ἀντίπατρος), ὁ,
Antipas: Rev.2:13.†
(AS)

11465.full:
κεραμικός, -ή, -όν
(κέραμος), [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:41 (פֶּחָר)* ;]
__1. (cl.) of a potter (e.g. γῆ).
__2. In LXX and NT, = cl., κεραμεοῦς (Plut., κεράμειος, Polyb., -μαῖος, etc), earthen: Rev.2:27.†
(AS)

11466.full:
ζεστός, -ή, -όν
(ζέω) [in Aq.: Lev.6:21; in Al.: Lev.7:12 * ;]
boiling hot (Strab., al.): metaphorically, Rev.3:15-16.†
(AS)

11467.full:
χλιαρός, -ά, -όν
(χλίω, to become warm),
warm, tepid; metaphorically, of persons, luke-warm: Rev.3:16.†
(AS)

s: an eye salve shaped like a roll
11469.full:
κολλούριον
(TTr., κολλύ-, the more usual form), -ου, τό (dimin. of κολλύρα = κόλλιξ, a coarse bread roll), [in LXX: 3Ki.12:24 hil B* ;]
__1. a small bread roll (LXX, ll. with).
__2. (Usually in pl., LS, see word) an eye salve shaped like a roll: Rev.3:18.†
(AS)

11470.full:
ζηλεύω,
late and rare form of ζηλόω, which see;
__1. to envy, be jealous.
__2. to be zealous: Rev.3:19.†
(AS)

11471.full:
σμαράγδινος
(σμάραγδος, which see),
__1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
__2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).†
(AS)

11473.full:
πυρρός -ά, -όν
(πῦρ) [in LXX for אֱדֹם ;]
fiery red: Rev.6:4 12:3.†
Πύρρος, -ου, ὁ,
Pyrrhus: Act.20:4.†
(AS)

11476.full:
ἄψινθος, -ου, ἡ
(also ἀψίνθιον, τό; ἀψινθία, ἡ),
wormwood: as a proper name, Rev.8:11.†
(AS)

11477.full:
μεσουράνημα, -τος, τό
(μεσουρανέω, to be in mid-heaven, of the sun at the meridian),
the zenith, mid-heaven: Rev.8:13 14:6 19:17.†
(AS)

11478.full:
Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדּוֹן, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: Job.26:6, 28:22, 31:12, Psa.88:12, Pro.15:11*), indecl.;
in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: Rev.9:11.†
(AS)

11481.full:
βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βιβλάριον, diminutive of βίβλος),
a little book: Rev.10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.†
(AS)

11482.full:
μυκάσμαι, -ῶμαι in cl. chiefly poët.,
[in Sm.: Job.6:5 * ;]
prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: Rev.10:3.†
(AS)

11483.full:
κατήγωρ, ὁ (Aram. קָטִיגוֺר; Dalman, Gr., 185; but see Deiss., LAE, 90 f.),
= κατήγορος,
an accuser: Rev.12:10.†
(AS)

11484.full:
ποταμο-φόρητος, -ον
carried away by a stream:
Rev.12:15 (for two exx. in π., see MM, xxi).†
(AS)

11485.full:
ἅρκος
(Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב ;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a bear: Rev.13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)†
(AS)

s: one who plays and sings to the lyre, a harper
11486.full:
κιθαρ-ωδός, -οῦ, ὁ
(κιθάρα, ἀοιδός, a singer)
one who plays and sings to the lyre, a harper: Rev.14:2 18:22.†
(AS)

11487.full:
μασάομαι (Rec. μασσ), -ῶμαι
(Aristoph. and late writers, but not in Trag. or in good Att.. prose), [in LXX: Job.30:4 (לֶחֶם), Sir.19:9 A * ;]
to bite, chew: Rev.16:10.†
(AS)

11490.full:
στρηνιάω, ῶ
(στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Isa.61:6 (אָכַל) * ;]
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Rev.18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω (AS)

11491.full:
σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν
(οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Rev.18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†
(AS)

11492.full:
θύινος (usually θύϊνος, as Rec.), -η, -ον
(θυία, θύα, an African aromatic tree, with ornamentally veined wood of varying colour, = Lat. citrinus), [in Sm.: 3Ki.10:11 (אַלְמֻגִּים)* ;]
thyme: ξύλον, Rev.18:12 (Diosc.).†
(AS)

s: amomum, a fragrant plant of India
11493.full:
ἄμωμον, -ου, τό,
amomum, a fragrant plant of India (RV, spice): Rev.18:13
(AS)

11497.full:
σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Rev.18:22.†
(AS)

11498.full:
πελεκίζω
(πέλεκυς, a battle-axe),
to out off with an axe, esp. to behead: with accusative, Rev.20:4 (Polyb., al.).†
(AS)

s: to shine like crystal, be crystal-clear
11499.full:
κρυσταλλίζω
(κρύσταλλος),
to shine like crystal, be crystal-clear: Rev.21:11 (ἅπ, λεγ.).†
(AS)
